stem: When coordinating immunologic monitoring for a kidney transplant recipient, which post-transplant test is supported by evolving antibody-detection technology in standard references?

options.text: Panel-reactive antibody (PRA) testing only after transplant with no pretransplant role
ABO typing repeated monthly solely to detect acute cellular rejection
Crossmatch testing only before procurement with no post-transplant monitoring

explanation.rationale_correct: Improved HLA antibody, PRA, and donor-specific antibody detection technologies support pretransplant sensitization assessment and post-transplant DSA monitoring as protocols evolve.

rationale_incorrect.B: PRA and HLA testing are emphasized prior to transplant to identify highly sensitized patients; DSA testing is specifically noted after transplant.
rationale_incorrect.C: ABO typing is part of compatibility assessment, not the evolving post-transplant antibody surveillance described.
rationale_incorrect.D: Post-transplant DSA testing is explicitly described alongside pretransplant PRA/HLA testing.

primary_anchor.section: Ch. 4, Pharmacology → Immunosuppressive Antibody Therapy → B.

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 4 → Immunosuppressive Antibody Therapy → B. (DSA testing after transplant alongside pretransplant PRA/HLA testing); PDF p. 134 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

notes: Source-first item. Post-transplant DSA angle distinct from hypercoagulability screening (cctc-2059) and intestine-failure definition (cctc-2064); anchor verified on Cupples p. 134.

stem: A highly sensitized heart transplant candidate is scheduled for pretransplant rituximab desensitization. Which long-term risk should the coordinator include in informed consent counseling per standard references?

options.text: Increased antibody-mediated rejection and post-transplant coronary artery vasculopathy with decreased graft survival
Guaranteed elimination of all donor-specific antibodies with no rejection risk
Rituximab desensitization is contraindicated in every heart transplant candidate
Desensitization permanently prevents coronary artery vasculopathy in all recipients

explanation.rationale_correct: Long-term data on pretransplant rituximab or plasmapheresis in highly sensitized recipients have shown increased antibody-mediated rejection and post-transplant coronary artery vasculopathy with decreased overall graft survival, although experience remains limited.

rationale_incorrect.B: Desensitization may improve crossmatch feasibility but does not guarantee antibody elimination or absence of rejection.
rationale_incorrect.C: Rituximab is used to desensitize selected heart candidates rather than being universally contraindicated.
rationale_incorrect.D: CAV risk may increase rather than being permanently prevented by desensitization.

primary_anchor.quote_hint: rituximab … increase in antibody-mediated rejection (AMR) and posttransplant coronary artery vasculopathy (CAV) and a decrease in overall graft survival

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 9 → desensitization → Rituximab → 3. (increased AMR and CAV with decreased graft survival); PDF p. 412 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

notes: Source-first item. First rituximab/desensitization item in bank; distinct from heart PRA crossmatch coordination (cctc-2026) and right-heart catheterization (cctc-2057); anchor verified on Cupples p. 412.

stem: When explaining simultaneous pancreas-kidney (SPK) transplantation to a candidate with diabetes and renal insufficiency, which indication aligns with standard references?

options.text: Diabetes or pancreatic exocrine insufficiency with renal insufficiency
Isolated type 2 diabetes without any renal disease
Renal insufficiency without any metabolic or pancreatic disorder
SPK is indicated only when the candidate no longer requires insulin

explanation.rationale_correct: Simultaneous pancreas-kidney transplantation is indicated for diagnosis of diabetes or pancreatic exocrine insufficiency with renal insufficiency.

rationale_incorrect.B: Type 2 diabetes accounts for a small minority of pancreas transplants; SPK pairs pancreatic and renal failure indications.
rationale_incorrect.C: SPK addresses combined pancreatic/metabolic and renal insufficiency rather than isolated renal disease alone.
rationale_incorrect.D: Insulin-treated diabetes with metabolic complications is typical of pancreas transplant populations rather than an exclusion.

primary_anchor.section: Ch. 15, Pancreas Transplantation → Indications → B. Simultaneous pancreas-kidney → 1.
primary_anchor.quote_hint: Diagnosis of diabetes or pancreatic exocrine insufficiency with renal insufficiency

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 15 → Indications → B. Simultaneous pancreas-kidney → 1. (diabetes or exocrine insufficiency with renal insufficiency); PDF p. 825 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

notes: Source-first item. SPK-indication angle distinct from SPK suitability (cctc-2038), PAK evaluation (cctc-2050), and SPK rejection combo (cctc-3016); anchor verified on Cupples p. 825.

stem: During preoperative coordination for a heart transplant candidate, which psychosocial support action aligns with standard heart transplant protocols?

options.text: Give the patient and family opportunity to ask questions and verbalize concerns
Discourage questions until one year after transplant to reduce anxiety
Limit all communication to the surgeon without involving caregivers
Defer emotional support until after hospital discharge only

explanation.rationale_correct: Heart preoperative protocols include providing emotional support by giving the patient and family opportunity to ask questions or verbalize their concerns.

rationale_incorrect.B: Preoperative protocols encourage questions and concern expression rather than deferring discussion.
rationale_incorrect.C: Caregiver involvement and open communication are part of preoperative emotional support.
rationale_incorrect.D: Emotional support is part of preoperative coordination, not deferred exclusively to post-discharge.

primary_anchor.section: Ch. 9, Heart Transplantation → preoperative coordination → J.
primary_anchor.quote_hint: Provide emotional support … Give patient/family opportunity to ask questions or verbalize their concerns

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 9 → preoperative coordination → J. (emotional support; opportunity to ask questions and verbalize concerns); PDF p. 412 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

notes: Source-first item. Heart preop emotional-support angle distinct from rituximab desensitization counseling (cctc-2066) and return-to-work postop counseling (cctc-3059); anchor verified on Cupples p. 412.
